extracted.intended_audience: Authors of systematic reviews and meta-analyses (healthcare), journal editors and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses using the PRISMA Statement (a 27‑item checklist and flow diagram); intended to improve completeness and transparency of reported reviews, especially randomized trials and evaluations of interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA 27-item checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRISMA Statement consists of a 27-item checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An evidence-based minimum set of items for reporting in systematic reviews and meta-analyses. The aim is to help authors improve the reporting of systematic reviews and meta-analyses. The checklist is the core reporting standard on this site and is the definitive version replacing the older QUOROM Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA four-phase flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRISMA Statement includes a four-phase flow diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the flow diagram to depict the flow of information through the different phases of a systematic review (e.g., identification, screening, eligibility, included). It complements the checklist to improve transparency of study selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the PRISMA Explanation and Elaboration document
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRISMA Explanation and Elaboration document explains and illustrates the principles underlying the PRISMA Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is strongly recommended that the Explanation and Elaboration document be used in conjunction with the PRISMA Statement for detailed interpretation, examples, and clarification of each checklist item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary focus on randomized trials but applicable beyond
rubrics_metrics.description: PRISMA has been focused on randomized trials, but can also be used as a basis for reporting systematic reviews of other types of research, particularly evaluations of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the checklist primarily to randomized trials but adapt items as appropriate for other study types and topics; recognize where specific items may need contextual interpretation for non-randomized research.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA is for reporting, not a methodological quality instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: PRISMA may be useful for critical appraisal of published systematic reviews, although it is not a quality assessment instrument to gauge the quality of a systematic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat adherence to PRISMA as a direct measure of methodological quality; use separate tools for risk of bias or methodological assessment when assessing review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register systematic review protocols at PROSPERO
rubrics_metrics.description: Register your systematic review protocols at PROSPERO (the first online facility to prospectively register systematic reviews via their protocol).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective registration of protocols is recommended to improve transparency and reduce risk of bias; PROSPERO is a global initiative led by the Centre for Reviews and Dissemination, University of York.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the current definitive version; PRISMA evolves
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRISMA Statement is an evolving document that is subject to change periodically as new evidence emerges. This website contains the current definitive version of the PRISMA Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always consult and apply the most recent version of PRISMA and related explanatory materials when preparing or appraising a systematic review.
